neighbours.label: the word just before 'as' in the concessive inversion 'ADJ/VERB as it was / as he might' (try as he might, unlikely as it seemed), placed mid-sentence, as against the same content in a plain 'but' clause
fire: The boy practised every day but, try as he might, he could not reach the top.
They searched the attic and, unlikely as it seemed, found the missing ring.
Her first draft was, rough as it was, the best thing she had written.
The old bridge held and, odd as it sounds, nobody was surprised.
We pushed the car for an hour but, try as we might, it would not start.
His plan was, crude as it may be, better than doing nothing.
The team lost again and, painful as it was, the coach praised them.
She kept the letter because, silly as it seems, it made her smile.
quiet: The boy practised every day, but he still could not reach the top.
They searched the attic and, to their surprise, found the missing ring.
Her first draft was rough, but it was the best thing she had written.
The old bridge held, and nobody was surprised by that.
We pushed the car for an hour, but it still would not start.
His plan was crude, but it was better than doing nothing.
The team lost again, and the coach still praised them.
She kept the letter because it always made her smile.
